Params: <size=40>The worship of titans runs through the entire human history.</size>
<size=40>From the vast mountains and seas to the endless expanse of the stars, humanity worships and fears all that lies beyond its understanding.</size>
<size=40>That worship and fear give rise to imitation. Once humanity gains enough power, it begins to build wonders of its own.</size>
<size=40>They are expected to be unbreakable, an anchor against the unknown; they are expected to outlast time itself, as proof of humanity's existence.</size>
<size=40>And yet, humanity pays prices it should never have to bear and makes sacrifices beyond all imagination for them.</size>
Now all those who once worshipped, feared, depended on, and possessed this wonder have sunk into the lightless deep. And here you are, an outsider, walking into its very heart.
This place has been classified from the very beginning. Only a handful of research teams were allowed to enter. I've never been here myself.
The two of you are on high alert, advancing cautiously through the vast steel-blue chamber.
Ananke's golden threads shoot out from every surface of the chamber walls, layering and intersecting at the very center.
The Ananke here is intact. The point where those threads converge must be the half of the "Understanding" Sefirah it's locked away.
Her deduction proves correct. You have seen the other half of "Understanding" back in Port Podesta, and it is easy to recognize that the thing suspended by those golden threads is what you came for.
Adelyde stops before the control panel and folds her arms, gazing up at the half-helix above. Her voice is a tangle of emotions.
It's hard to believe something so small could bring about two catastrophes. It gave us our home, and took away everything we had.
Don't get too close. It's best we don't directly contact "Understanding".
In Port Podesta, Helentine experienced how it overloads the mind.
A realization flickers across Adelyde's face.
And you've seen what the Consciousness Tide surges did to people during the Atlantic Calamity.
Rashly using "Understanding" to control the Consciousness Tide... even Arius would struggle to hold onto himself.
This place was built specifically to analyze "Understanding". By that logic, there should be a containment vessel designed to house and transfer it beyond this cube.
One step at a time. We can't restart Ananke and extract the Sefirah until the other teams have completed their objectives.
Once the Sefirah is extracted, Arius could strike at any time.
He will have the element of surprise. Our best move is to buy time and hold out until our forces can close in.
A fully-formed plan is transmitted from the other end of the M.I.N.D. connection.
Her gaze sweeps across the dark mechanical dome before settling on the brilliant streams of Ananke rays within the cube. Something molten stirs behind her eyes.
To wait patiently and vigilantly, then strike hard and fast when the moment comes—that is the mark of every F.O.S. commandant.
The silver-white Ascendant's true strength remains unknown, but that uncertainty does not lessen the preparedness of you and Adelyde.
By the time the two of you have the terrain mapped out, your comms finally crackle to life.
Across the terminal screen, an impressive web of connections comes into view.
Commander: all three Comet sub-units are activated.
The sub-unit in server room 41 is activated.
The sub-unit in the Consciousness Tide Lab is activated.
The sub-unit in Current Ecology Station One is activated.
The reconstruction key has been entered in the Ananke main control room.
Once, all that came through those connections were dying whispers.
Those who came after now stand where their predecessors' convictions still echo, kindling that golden sea of stars once more.
At the edge of your vision, the sigil marking Ananke's highest administrative access once again glows as brightly as it did decades ago.
Standing shoulder to shoulder with you at the control panel, Adelyde turns and breaks into a smile of pure, unguarded excitement.
The moment your palm meets the sensor panel, the entire cabin lightly shakes.
A hum resonates from somewhere deep inside, and the Atlantic Eye stirs slowly from its long slumber.
Streams of light surge and swell, and the ocean that breeds the Phylotree greets you with a resonant chord.
The instant the command is given, golden rays burst outward from the engine bay, racing through every steel beam and framework.
Intensity of Ananke rays is rising across all areas.
This is the Balder observation team. The energy surges outside are diminishing. The Red Tide has stopped spreading!
The teams on the other end of the comms erupt with excitement, but your other hand stays clenched beneath the control panel, your palm cold and slick with sweat.
The hardest part is only just beginning. It stares back at you from the screen ahead.
All your senses expand beyond their limits. You can trace the path of every strand of light as it pulls away from the Sefirah.
The crystalline half-helix returns to the world from the frozen spacetime, stirring once more beneath the breathless gazes of the two of you.
And then, all information of this world is revealed to you at once.
It is as if you can grasp the entire workings of the Atlantic Eye and decide whether it crumbles or gets rebuilt with a single thought.
It is as if every secret and hidden current lurking within Babylonia lies completely exposed to you, and every heart laid open for you to guide or manipulate at will.
The language of the Punishing Virus, the laws of the Phylotree, even fate itself have removed their veils, whispering a silent plea to you—
Maybe we've been overlooking something all along.
The Sefirah is a crystallization of some facet of human nature. Perhaps it has a nature of its own, one that yearns to be used to unlock omniscience.
Adelyde speaks softly, her silhouette almost unreal against the luminous blue haze. Even you have no idea what "Understanding" whispered to her.
I've seen what becomes of those who chase omniscience.
If wandering every wrong path has taught us anything at all, it's this...
You don't have to understand everything to do what's right.

The halo recedes from her red frame, its restless rhythm slowly turning to stillness. As the last golden thread withdraws, a small sealed capsule rises from the cubic base, drawing the half of "Understanding" inside.
Adelyde steps forward, counting down in silence alongside you.
She lunges forward and grabs the capsule.

A bolt of blue lightning suddenly strikes from the distance. Adelyde swings her cannon behind to block it before retreating with you and the capsule, stopping just at the edge of her cannon's maximum range.
She rises, turns, and plants herself between you and the threat. Rage burns through from somewhere deep within her frame.
Don't you have anything to say for yourself, Rusalka?!
